overview.title: Help
overview.body:
**What I'm here for**
- I watch Twitch chat for you and ping this Discord place when something interesting happens.
- I can also react to live/offline changes and, if you want, even write in Twitch chat for you.
- Every Discord channel, thread, or DM has its own setup.
  So whatever you change here stays here.

**How I feel best to use**
- Most of the time, just open the normal command and let me show you the UI.
  `/channel`, `/user`, `/ping`, `/reply`, `/liveping`, `/permission`, `/account`, `/write`, and `/show` all work great like that.
- Direct parameters are more of a fast lane.
  They feel best once you already know exactly what you want or when your lists get pretty big.

**The usual beginner route**
- Start with `/join` so I may work in this Discord place.
- Add your Twitch channels with `/channel`.
- Build your first pings with `/ping`.
- Add `/reply`, `/liveping`, `/account`, or `/write` later when you want the fancier stuff.

**If you want details**
- `/show` lets me show you what is saved here right now.
- `/help section:...` jumps straight into a topic like `pings`, `auto_replies`, or `tips`.

first_steps.title: Help: First Steps
first_steps.body:
**How I would set myself up first**
- Run `/join` where you want me to work.
- If needed, switch my language with `/language`.
- Add at least one Twitch channel with `/channel`.
- Create your first ping with `/ping`.
- If you want to double-check everything, let me show it with `/show`.

**My favorite first test**
- Track one Twitch channel.
- Make one easy ping for your own name or another simple word.
- Then wait for a matching Twitch message and see if I ping here like I should.

**What can wait until later**
- Users, replies, permissions, account linking, and live pings are nice extras.
- First I should simply watch a channel and send one clean Discord ping.

channels.title: Help: Channels
channels.body:
**What channels mean to me**
- Tracked channels are the Twitch channels I'm supposed to care about here.
- They are the base for normal pings, live/offline pings, and manual Twitch writes.

**How I want you to use this**
- Open `/channel` without parameters and let my UI guide you.
- Add every Twitch channel I should watch here.
- Remove the ones I should stop caring about.

**One useful thing to know**
- If a channel is still used by saved pings, I will not just drop it.
  Then you first need to remove or change those pings.

users.title: Help: Users
users.body:
**What users mean to me**
- Tracked users are optional little memory helpers for me.
- They matter when a ping should only care about specific Twitch names.

**When this gets cool**
- You want me to react only to one streamer, mod, friend, or known username.
- You want certain people excluded from triggering a ping.

**When you can skip it**
- If you do not care who wrote the Twitch message, you can ignore `/user` completely.

**How I use saved users later**
- Add them with `/user`.
- Then pick them inside `/ping` when you want to narrow a ping down to certain people.

pings.title: Help: Pings
pings.body:
**What a ping is to me**
- A ping is one thing I'm supposed to look for in Twitch chat.
- If I see it, I send a Discord message here.

**How I like pings best**
- Open `/ping` without parameters and build it through my UI.
- Start with a normal word ping when you can.
  Regex is there for the fancy cases.

**What you can make me care about**
- Which Twitch channels may trigger it
- Which users may trigger it
- Whether subscriber state matters
- Whether I should trigger while the streamer is live, offline, or both
- Optional color and priority

**Easy starter ideas**
- Your own username
- A team or clan tag
- A short phrase you really want to catch

**If you want more**
- If I should also write in Twitch chat after a ping match, add `/reply` on top.

auto_replies.title: Help: Auto-Replies
auto_replies.body:
**What auto-replies let me do**
- Auto-replies let me write in Twitch chat for you automatically.
- I can do that after a normal ping match or after a live/offline event.

**When this is worth it**
- You want a Twitch response without typing it yourself every time.
- You want me to post something when a tracked channel goes live or offline.

**What I need first**
- I need a linked Twitch account for this.
- If you only want Discord pings, you can ignore auto-replies completely.

**The easy way to think about it**
- `/ping` or `/liveping` tells me when I should react.
- `/reply` tells me what I should say in Twitch chat.

live_pings.title: Help: Live Pings
live_pings.body:
**What live pings are to me**
- Live pings tell me to post here when a tracked Twitch channel goes live.
- Offline pings tell me to post again when that channel goes offline.

**Why people usually like them**
- They are perfect when this Discord place should know when a stream starts or ends.
- They also let different tracked channels have their own little live/offline moments.

**How I want them set up**
- Add the Twitch channel first with `/channel`.
- Then open `/liveping` and choose `Live` or `Offline`.
- If you want, give them colors so they stand out more.

**One important detail**
- If I should also say something in Twitch chat on those events, add an event auto-reply afterwards.

write.title: Help: Write
write.body:
**What `/write` lets me do**
- `/write` lets me send one manual Twitch chat message for you through the linked account.
- It is great for quick tests or for messages you want to send right now on purpose.

**When this feels useful**
- You want to test whether I can write to Twitch correctly.
- You want to send something without waiting for a ping or event.
- You want to reply directly to a recent Twitch message.

**What I need first**
- I need a linked Twitch account.
- If I do not have one yet, start with `/account`.

account.title: Help: Account
account.body:
**What I use the linked Twitch account for**
- I only need a linked Twitch account when I should write in Twitch chat.
- That means `/write` and every kind of auto-reply.

**When you can ignore this**
- If you only want Discord notifications, pings, and live/offline notices, you do not need `/account` at all.

**How I want this done**
- Open `/account` and choose `Connect`.
- Finish the Twitch login.
- Then come back and use `/reply` or `/write` with me.

**Nice detail**
- If you disconnect the account, I keep your saved replies.
- I just cannot send Twitch messages again until another account is linked.

permissions.title: Help: Permissions
permissions.body:
**What permissions mean to me**
- Permissions decide who else may manage me in this Discord place.
- They are useful when more than one person should be allowed to work on the setup.

**When you can ignore them**
- If this setup is yours alone, `/permission` is usually not a big deal.

**How I like permissions best**
- Give small permissions when someone should only help with one part.
- Give `admin` only when someone should really be allowed to do everything.
- Use `Clear` when you want me to forget all special permissions for one user again.

tips.title: Help: Helpful Tips
tips.body:
**My favorite tricks**
- Ask an AI to build or explain regex for you.
  Just tell it exactly what I should match and what I should ignore.
- `.*` as a regex matches every single message.
  If you mix that with channel and/or user filters, you can make me watch one specific person on one specific channel.
- `^Your text$` matches one full message exactly.
  I really recommend that for auto-replies so I do not trigger on extra words.
- `^!song$` is a great example for command-like auto-replies.
  That makes me react only to the exact message `!song`.
- `hello|hi|hey` lets one ping match several alternatives.
- `\\bword\\b` matches a real whole word.
  That helps when `cat` should not also match `catch` or `educate`.
- If a regex gets too wild, do not force everything into one giant pattern.
  It often feels much cleaner to keep the regex simple and narrow me down with user, channel, subscriber, or live/offline filters.
